再说，倘若这些东西真像它们被说成的那样——不过是些稻草人——那么对兵工厂、要塞、演习等等的热衷还维持得下去吗？花在它们身上的全部钱财，就只是为了它们永远不被使用？各国人民就该被迫掏出全部的钱，在国境上修筑堡垒，好隔着堡垒互相行吻手礼吗？军队就这样降格为一支维持和平的宪兵，『至高无上的军阀』就只该统率一群永远的避战者吗？不；在这副面具——『欲和平，先备战』（si vis pacem）的面具——后面，会心的眼色彼此闪烁，那些表决通过每一笔战争预算的议员们，也同时在递着眼色。」

「人民的代表怎么了？」部长插进来。「这种在危难时节从不含糊的牺牲精神，这种在一致通过有关法令时的欢欣表现，难道不是只配赞美吗？」

「恕我直言，大人阁下。我真想对那些一致举手的表决者一个一个地喊：『你那声「同意」，将夺走哪位母亲唯一的骨肉。你那声「同意」，将把哪个可怜人的双眼打出眶。你那声「同意」，将烧掉一座无可替代的藏书。你那声「同意」，将砸碎一位本会成为你国家荣耀的诗人的脑袋。可你们全都「同意」了这些，只为免得显得像个懦夫，仿佛表示赞同时唯一需要害怕的，只是关系到自己的那点事。』人的利己心难道大到这个地步，以致反对战争能想得出的动机就只剩这一个？好吧，我承认利己心确实大：因为你们每一位，都宁可驱赶十万人去毁灭，也不肯让亲爱的自己沾上一丁点儿『曾经害怕过一回』的嫌疑。」

「我希望，好医生，」上校冷冷地说，「您永远别去当议员；全院都会把您嘘下去。」

「哦，肯去冒这个险，本身就足以证明我不是懦夫了。逆流而泳，才需要钢铁的气力。」

「可万一危险时刻来了，我们发现自家毫无准备呢？」

===Original===

“Let such a condition of justice be instituted as would make the occurrence of ‘the moment of danger’ an impossibility. For what such a moment might be, colonel, no one can at present form any clear conception. With the dreadfulness of the science of warlike implements which we have already attained, and which is constantly advancing, with the enormous proportions of the powers engaged in the contest, the next war will in reality be no mere ‘moment of danger.’ But there is really no word for it. A time of gigantic misery﻿—aid and nursing out of the question﻿—sanitary reforms and the arrangements for provisioning will appear as mere irony in face of the demands upon them. The next war, about which people talk so glibly and so indifferently, will not be a gain for one side and loss for the other, but *ruin* for *all*. Who amongst us here votes for this ‘moment of danger’?”
“Not I, to be sure,” said the Minister, “and not you either, dear doctor; but men in general, and not our Government﻿—I will be surety for them﻿—but the other states.”
“What right have you to think other men worse and more unreasonable than you or I? Now I will tell you a little story:﻿—
“Before the closed gate of a beautiful garden stood a crowd of men, one thousand and one in number, looking in very longingly. The gatekeeper had orders to let the people in, in case the majority among them wished for admission. He called one of them to him, ‘Tell me﻿—only speak honestly﻿—do you wish to come in?’ ‘Oh yes, to be sure I do; but the other thousand, I am certain, do not.’ The careful gatekeeper wrote this answer in his notebook. Then he called up a second. He said the same. Again the other entered in the ‘Yes’ column the number 1, and in the ‘No’ column the number 1000. And so it went on up to the last man. Then he added up the figures. The result was﻿—one thousand and one ‘Yes’; over a million ‘No.’ So the gate remained shut, for the ‘Noes’ had a crushing majority; and that proceeded from the fact that everyone considered himself obliged to answer for the others too, instead of for himself only.”
“To be sure,” began the Minister thoughtfully; and again Lori Griesbach turned her eyes on him with admiration.

===Chinese===

「那就建立那样一种公义的秩序，让『危险时刻』的发生成为不可能。至于那样的时刻究竟会是什么，上校，眼下谁也无法形成清晰的构想。以我们已经达到、而且还在不断精进的战争器械科学的可怖，以投入角逐的各国力量的庞大比例，下一场战争实际上将远不止是一个『危险时刻』。那真是没有字眼可以形容的。一个浩大苦难的时代——救护与看护无从谈起——卫生改良与给养安排，在落在它们头上的需求面前将形同讽刺。下一场战争——人们对它谈得那样轻巧、那样无所谓——将不是一方得、一方失，而是全体的毁灭。我们这里有谁为这个『危险时刻』投赞成票？」

「我自然不投，」部长说，「您也不投，亲爱的医生；可是一般人就会——倒不是我们政府，这个我给他们作保——是别国。」

「您有什么权利认定别人就比您我更坏、更不讲理？好，我给您讲个小故事：——

「一座美丽花园的紧闭的园门前，站着一群人，数目一千零一，都眼巴巴朝里望着。守门人奉命：倘若人群中多数愿意进，就放他们进去。他唤过其中一人：『告诉我——只许说老实话——你想进来吗？』『哦，想，当然想；可那一千个，我敢肯定，都不想。』谨慎的守门人把这个回答记进小本子。接着唤第二个人。说的还是同样的话。守门人又在「是」栏记下 1，在「否」栏记下 1000。如此一直问到最后一个人。然后他合计算了算。结果是——一千零一个「是」；一百多万个「否」。于是园门依旧紧闭，因为「否」占了压倒的多数；而这都是因为人人认为自己有义务替别人作答，却不替自己作答。」

「那当然，」部长若有所思地开口；洛莉·格里斯巴赫又一次用倾慕的目光望着他。

===Original===

“To be sure, it would be a fine thing if a unanimous vote in favour of laying down one’s arms could be brought about; but, on the other side, what Government would dare to make the beginning? To be sure, there is nothing so desirable as concord; but, on the other side, how can lasting concord be thought possible so long as human passions, separate interests, and so forth, still continue?”
“I beg your pardon,” said my son Rudolf, now taking the word. “Forty millions of inhabitants in a state form one whole. Then why not several hundred millions? Can this be susceptible of logical and mathematical proof, that so long as human passions, separate interests, and so forth, still continue, it is indeed possible for forty millions of people to renounce the right to go to war with each other about them; nay, three states, like the present triple alliance, may ally themselves together, and form a ‘League of Peace’; but five states cannot do it, and must not do it. Truly, truly, our world of today gives itself out as wondrous wise, and laughs at the savages; and yet in many things we also cannot count up to five.”
Some voices made themselves heard: “What?” “Savages?” “That about us, with our overrefined culture?” “At the end of the nineteenth century?”
Rudolf stood up.
“Yes; savages. I will not recall the word. And so long as we cling to the past we shall remain savages. But we are already standing at the gate of a new period. Glances are directed forwards. All are pressing on strongly towards another, a higher form. Savagery, with its idols and its weapons﻿—there are many who are already edging away gradually from it. If even we may be nearer to barbarism than most people believe, we are also perhaps nearer to our ennoblement than most people hope. *The prince or statesman is perhaps already alive* who is to bring to perfection the exploit which will live in all future history as the most glorious and most enlightened of all exploits﻿—that which will carry universal disarmament. We have placed our feet already on the threshold of an age in which manhood is to raise itself into humanity﻿—to the nobility of humanity, as Frederick Tilling used to say.

===Chinese===

「那当然，倘若真能促成一致表决赞成放下武器，那是天大的好事；可是另一方面，哪个政府敢开头呢？那当然，再没有比和睦更可欲的了；可是另一方面，只要人类的情欲、各自的利益等等还在延续，怎么可能指望持久的和睦呢？」

「恕我冒昧，」我儿子鲁道夫这时开了腔。「一个国家四千万居民结成一个整体。那么为什么不能几万万结成一个？这在逻辑上、在数学上能证明吗——只要人类的情欲、各自的利益等等还在延续，四千万人就的确可以为着它们互相放弃开战的权利；不但如此，三个国家，像如今的三国同盟，还能结成「和平同盟」；而五个国家就不能，也不许。真的，真的，我们今天这个世界自以为聪明绝顶，笑话野蛮人；可是在许多事情上，我们自己也不会数到五。」

几处声音响起来：「什么？」「野蛮人？」「说我们，凭着我们过分精致的文明？」「都到十九世纪末了？」

鲁道夫站了起来。

「是的；野蛮人。我不收回这个词。而且只要我们还抱住过去不放，我们就还是野蛮人。可我们已经站在一个新时期的门口了。目光都朝前望去。一切都在奋力奔向另一种更高的形态。野蛮，连同它的偶像和它的武器——已经有许多人正从它旁边悄悄地渐行渐远。即便我们离野蛮可能比多数人以为的更近，我们或许也离我们的高尚化比多数人希望的更近。那位亲王或政治家也许已经活在世上，他将完成那桩将载入全部未来史册、堪称一切功业中最光荣、最开明的功业——普遍裁军的功业。我们已经把脚踏上了一个时代的门槛：在那个时代里，男子气概将升华为人性——升华为人性的高贵，弗雷德里克·蒂林从前常这样说。

===Original===

Mother, I drink this glass now to the memory of your unforgotten, loved, and trusted one, to whom I too owe everything, all I think and all I am; and from that glass (and he threw it against the wall, where it shattered to pieces) shall no other drop ever be drunk again; and today, at my newborn child’s christening, shall no other toast be proposed than *this*﻿—‘Hail to the future!’ To fulfil its tasks shall we clothe ourselves in steel? No. Shall we endeavour to show ourselves worthy of our fathers’ fathers, as the old phrase goes? No. But of our grandsons’ grandsons. Mother,” said he, breaking off, “you are weeping. What is the matter with you? What do you see there?”
My gaze had been directed to the open glass door. The rays of the setting sun had thrown a halo of tremulous gold round a rosebush, and from this, rising up in lifelike clearness, was my dream-picture. I saw the garden-shears glitter, the white hair shine. He smiled at me as he said, “Are we not a happy old couple?”
Ah, woe is me!
Finis.

===Chinese===

母亲，现在我饮下这一杯，纪念您那永不忘怀的、挚爱的、信靠的人——我所思所是的一切，也都是拜他所赐；（说着他把酒杯掷向墙壁，杯子在那里摔得粉碎）从那只杯子里，永远不许再饮下另一滴酒；而在今天，在我新生孩子的洗礼上，除了这一杯，再不许提议任何祝酒——『向未来欢呼！』完成未来的任务，需要我们披上钢铁吗？不。我们要努力证明自己无愧于我们的祖辈，像那句老话说的吗？不。而是无愧于我们孙辈的孙辈。母亲，」他顿住话头，「您哭了。您怎么了？您在那边看见了什么？」

我的目光原本正对着敞开的玻璃门。落日的余晖给一丛玫瑰围上一圈颤动的金色光晕，而从那光晕里，以栩栩如生的清晰，升起了我梦中的那幅图景。我看见园艺剪闪着光，看见白发亮着。他微笑着对我说：「我们不是一对幸福的老夫妻吗？」

啊，我这苦命的人啊！

终。
